Evidence Gate verdict by persona_validation_2: PASSED (S1 verified).

verified_insights: Across N=45,335 MAG papers (1954-2014), mean disruption declines from 0.0140 (percentile 54.3) for solo authors to 0.0004 (percentile 41.2) for 11+ teams (OLS slope -0.00187/author, p=6.89e-40), while mean citations rise from 24.0 to 68.1.
Within-field demeaning across 19 MAG Level-0 disciplines preserves the negative team-size vs. disruption gradient.
ruled_out_explanations: Ruled out composition across disciplines as the sole driver: field-demeaned disruption remains positive for solo authors and negative for large teams.
Ruled out post-2014 right-truncation as creating the historical negative slope: restricting strictly to 1954-2004 (>=17y forward window) retains the monotonic decline.
open_questions: Cross-corpus generalization to USPTO patents and GitHub software repositories from Nature 2019 was not re-run in this MAG/OpenAlex slice.
Recent counter-arguments (e.g., citation inflation & reference-list length biases in 2024-2026 preprints) warrant controlled reference-count normalization in S3.
methodology_lessons: Dataverse Aggregated_20210521.txt contains 6 columns (no Multi-Institution flag despite dataset prose abstract); empirical schema inspection prevented silent column-shift bugs.
Comparing 1954-2004 vs. 2015-2021 regimes shows forward citation-window truncation compresses D-score variance, confirming that cohort year fixed effects or matched windows are mandatory.
